quickStart.item_09: For an immediate emergency in Ireland, call 112 or 999.
quickStart.item_19: For public poison advice, call the National Poisons Information Centre on 01 809 2166 from 8am to 10pm. In an emergency call 112 or 999.
quickStart.item_20: For someone to talk to, call Samaritans free on 116 123, day or night.
quickStart.item_58: Review emergency contacts, health information, legal document locations, insurance, bank accounts, pensions, and essential liabilities.
quickStart.item_32: If someone has died, identify the executor or authorised representative and use the current Courts Service, Revenue, HSE, and provider procedures.
quickStart.item_42: Keep the export encrypted. Never put passwords, PINs, MyGovID or Revenue Online Service credentials, authentication codes, or recovery keys in it.

legalNotes.item_42: Ireland means the Republic of Ireland; Northern Ireland is part of the United Kingdom and follows different systems and laws.
legalNotes.item_102: PPS numbers are sensitive personal data. The Department of Social Protection says a PPS number has 7 digits followed by one or two letters; share it only with authorised bodies when needed.
legalNotes.item_49: Medical cards and GP visit cards have their own HSE eligibility requirements; do not assume every resident is entitled to a card or identical public coverage.
legalNotes.item_118: The Courts Service explains that probate or administration may be required. Revenue forms and tax steps depend on the date of death and estate facts.
legalNotes.item_41: Ireland has Capital Acquisitions Tax (CAT) on gifts and inheritances; tax thresholds, reliefs, filing, and payment depend on the facts and current Revenue rules.
legalNotes.item_05: An enduring power of attorney and advance healthcare directive are separate Decision Support Service arrangements. Confirm registration, activation, and authority before relying on a document.
legalNotes.item_104: Public-service guidance: practical arrangements after a death: https://www.citizensinformation.ie/en/death/practical-arrangements-after-a-death/
legalNotes.item_16: Decision Support Service: enduring power of attorney: https://www.decisionsupportservice.ie/services/enduring-power-attorney-epa
legalNotes.item_15: Decision Support Service: advance healthcare directives: https://www.decisionsupportservice.ie/services/advance-healthcare-directives

recoveryRoadmap.description: A general checklist after a death in Ireland. Confirm the representative's authority and current legal, tax, and provider requirements before acting.

meta.title: Family Recovery Roadmap - Ireland
meta.reviewedBy: Government and public-service sources reviewed; case-specific legal and tax advice may be needed

intro.condolence: We are sorry for your loss. This checklist is intended to make the first practical steps clearer.
intro.howToUse: Register the death, identify the executor or administrator, notify relevant agencies and providers, and keep a record of each action.

startHere.0: Register the death and obtain the records requested by the relevant organisations.
startHere.1: Locate the will and identify the executor; confirm whether a grant of representation is required.
startHere.2: Contact Revenue, the Department of Social Protection, banks, insurers, employers, pension providers, and utilities as appropriate.
startHere.3: List assets, debts, regular payments, and claims; confirm responsibility before changing payments or distributing property.
startHere.4: Keep a log of contacts, forms, and documents supplied. Do not use the deceased person's online credentials or accounts without authority.

legalFramework.0: Courts Service probate and grant-of-representation procedures.
legalFramework.1: Revenue income tax, CAT, probate-related forms, and estate obligations.
legalFramework.2: Decision Support Service enduring powers of attorney and advance healthcare directives.
legalFramework.3: State pensions, occupational pension scheme rules, insurance contracts, and beneficiary nominations.

2.focus: Complete required court, Revenue, property, and provider steps before final distribution.

cat.note: Revenue provides current CAT rules, thresholds, forms, and reliefs. Do not rely on a static amount in this guide.

0.definition: A court grant authorising an executor or administrator to deal with an estate; the grant type and whether one is required depend on the case.

1.definition: Irish tax that may apply to gifts or inheritances. Liability, thresholds, reliefs, and filing duties depend on circumstances and current Revenue rules.

2.definition: A Decision Support Service arrangement that can authorise a trusted person to act on certain decisions if the donor loses capacity, subject to registration and legal requirements.
